valueString.value: NL-PS level 4b: bearer token from your own system for your level 4b test patient

title.value: NL-PS-L4-B - Level 4b: Two maximal GBBs per section - XML Format

description.value: The serving system provides an NL-PS for its level 4b test patient, in which every mandatory section except Medication summary has at least two entries, each with a maximal generic building block (GBB), and has a narrative, and Medication summary has no entries, and has an emptyReason and a narrative. Conformancelab sends the bearer token you enter at test setup to your server. Use a token issued by your own system that gives access to your level 4b test patient, and only to that patient. Without a token the server may return the Patient Summaries of several patients; the script then tests the first one. Implementation Guides: NL-PS https://ig.nictiz.nl/nlps/ and generic building blocks (GBB) https://ig.nictiz.nl/gbb/
The id of the first Patient Summary Composition in the search result.
Search the NL-PS Composition of the test patient.
Search the Patient Summary Compositions of the patient: GET [base]/Composition?type=http://loinc.org|60591-5
Confirm that the operation was successful
Confirm that the response is a searchset Bundle.
Confirm that the search result contains at least one Patient Summary Composition. Without one, step 2 cannot run.

Confirm that the search result contains exactly one Patient Summary. If there are more, step 2 uses the first one in the order of the server: check the Composition id in the request of step 2 to see which one was tested. Use a token that only gives access to one test patient to avoid this.

name.value: Retrieve and check Patient Summary document

description.value: Retrieve the NL-PS as a document Bundle with $document and check the document as a whole. Check that every mandatory section except Medication summary has at least two entries, each with a maximal generic building block (GBB), and has a narrative, and Medication summary has no entries, and has an emptyReason and a narrative.
Retrieve the Patient Summary as a document: GET [base]/Composition/[id]/$document
Confirm that the operation was successful
Confirm that the response is a Bundle.
Confirm that the Bundle is a document. (FHIR R4 allows a server to wrap the document in a searchset Bundle; that is not accepted here.)
Confirm that the first entry of the document is a Composition.
Confirm that the Composition is a Patient Summary (type LOINC 60591-5).

Confirm that the document conforms to http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Bundle, and its resources to the profiles they claim in meta.profile. A resource without meta.profile, such as the Patient or a GBB entry, is only validated against the base FHIR specification for now.

Confirm that the Composition conforms to http://ig.nictiz.nl/nlps/StructureDefinition/nl-PatientSummary, and through it to the EU-PS profile it imposes. The Composition does not need to claim the profile in meta.profile.
Section Problems (LOINC 11450-4): the section is present.
Section Allergies and intolerances (LOINC 48765-2): the section is present.
Section Medication summary (LOINC 10160-0): the section is present.
Section History of procedures (LOINC 47519-4): the section is present.
Section Medical devices (LOINC 46264-8): the section is present.
Section Problems (LOINC 11450-4): the section has at least 2 entries.
Section Problems (LOINC 11450-4): every entry refers to a Condition in the document.

expression.value: Bundle.entry.first().resource.where($this is Composition).section.where(code.coding.where(system = 'http://loinc.org' and code = '11450-4').exists()).all(entry.reference.subsetOf(%resource.entry.where(resource is Condition).select(fullUrl | ('Condition/' + resource.id))))
